When the three birds, the powerful ones, came together with the threefold [hymn] toward the single syllable, they warded off death with immortality, shielding themselves from all misfortunes.
May the green [bird] protect you from heaven; may the white [bird] protect you from the mid-space.
May this iron one protect you from the earth; may it go forth as this citadel of the gods.
(9) These three citadels of the gods—may they protect you on every side.
Wearing them, may you be radiant and superior to your enemies. (10)
The city of the gods, the immortal gold, which the first god fastened in the beginning—to him I pay homage with ten eastern [fingers]; may he grant his approval for my triple-fastening.
May Aryaman, Pūṣan, and Bṛhaspati draw you tight.
With that name which was given to you at birth, we release you from it.
(12) With the seasons and the seasonal periods, for the sake of life and luster; with the splendor of the year, we make your jaw strong. (13)
Drawn from clarified butter, anointed with honey, firm as the earth, unshakable, and bringing us across;
splitting our rivals and casting them down, ascend me for great good fortune!
Yoked in front, O Jātavedas, carry [the sacrifice]; O Agni, know this which is being performed.
(5.29.1.c) You are the physician; you are the maker of the remedy. Through you, may we win cattle, horses, and men.

(5.29.2’) O Agni Jātavedas, acting in concert with all the gods, do that for us: (5.29.2.c) [Ensure] that whoever has played us false, whoever has devoured us—so that he shall fall into his own enclosure.
O Agni Jātavedas, act in such a way that it shall fall into his enclosing-sticks;
do this in harmony with all the gods.
Pierce his two eyes, pierce his heart, cut out his tongue, and crush his teeth!
(5.29.4.c) O Agni, youngest one, crush back whichever Piśāca has devoured him!

(5.29.5’) Whatever of his has been carried off, scattered, or taken away, whatever has been eaten by the Piśācas from his own body—O Agni, you who know, bring that back; we shall infuse flesh and life-breath into his body.

Whether in raw food, well-cooked, mixed, or thoroughly ripened, whatever Piśāca has harmed me while eating—that Piśāca shall depart by himself along with his offspring; let this man be free from disease.
Whatever [Piśāca] has harmed me in milk or in churned curds, or in grain that ripens after being ploughed—whatever [has harmed me] in food—[let him depart].
(5.29.7.c) May the Piśācas depart from that, along with their own selves and their offspring; may this man be free from disease.

(5.29.8.a) Whosoever among the flesh-eating sorcerers has harmed me while I was drinking water, or while I was lying down upon my bed— (5.29.8.c) may the Piśācas depart from that, along with their own selves and their offspring; may this man be free from disease.

Whether by day or by night, whichever flesh-eater among the sorcerers has harmed me as I lay upon my bed—let those *piśācas* depart from themselves and their offspring; let this man be free from disease.
O Agni, Jātavedas, slay the flesh-eating, blood-drinking *piśāca* who steals away the mind!
(5.29.10.c) May Indra, the prize-winner, strike him with his thunderbolt; may Soma boldly cut off his head.
(5.29.11’) From of old, O Agni, you have crushed the sorcerers; the demons have never conquered you in battles.
(5.29.11.c) Burn up the flesh-eaters along with their roots; let them not escape your divine weapon.
Gather together, O Jātavedas, whatever has been taken and whatever has been brought away;
may his limbs grow, and may this man swell like a stalk of soma. Like a stalk of soma, O Jātavedas, may this man swell.
(5.29.13.c) O Agni, make him vigorous, pure, and free from disease; let him live!
(5.29.14’) These, O Agni, are your fuel-sticks that crush the Piśācas;
do you accept them and take them up, O Jātavedas! (5.29.14.c) 14.
O Agni, accept these fuel-sticks with your flame, [the wood] of the *tārṣṭāghī* tree.
Let the flesh-eater abandon his form, he who seeks to seize this man’s flesh.
From near at hand, from afar, from every direction, come to us!
Stay right here; do not go away, and do not follow after your ancestors. I bind your life-force firmly.
Whether it be a man of your own kin or a stranger who has cast a spell upon you—I utter for you both the words of release and complete liberation.
Whatever offense you have committed against a woman or a man through thoughtlessness,
or whatever you have sinned— whether it be an act toward your mother or an act toward your father— I declare both the release and the full liberation for you with my speech.
(5.30.4.c) Both the unloosing and the releasing—I declare them both to you with my speech.
(5.30.5’) Whatever your mother, whatever your father, your kin, and your brother have brought upon you—turn toward this medicine; I make you one who reaches old age.
(5.30.5.c) Turn toward the remedy; I make you one who attains full longevity.
Stay here, O man, with your whole mind;
do not follow the two messengers of Yama. Go toward the dwellings of the living!
Summoned back, return once more, you who know the way of departure.
(5.30.7.c) It is an ascent, an advance, the path for the living and the living.
(5.30.8.a) Do not fear; you shall not die. I make you reach old age.
(5.30.8.c) I have driven away the consumption from your limbs, the fever of your body.
The breaking of your limbs, the fever in your members, and that disease of your heart— the consumption has flown away like a hawk, struck down by my word, far beyond.
The seers Bodha and Pratibodha, Asvapna and Jāgṛvi—
May those two, the guardians of your vital breath, remain awake by day and by night.
(10) This fire has been attended; here let the sun rise for you.
Arise from the deep death, even from the black darkness! (11)
Homage to Yama, homage be to Death; homage to the Fathers and those who lead [the dead].
I place that Agni at my front, he who knows the crossing over, for our safety and well-being.
May breath come back, may mind come back, may sight and likewise strength come back.
(5.30.13.c) May his body be restored; may it stand firm upon its two feet.
(5.30.14’) O Agni, unite him with breath and sight; quicken him with body and strength.
(5.30.14.c) You know the path of immortality; let him not go astray, let him not become one who dwells in the earth. (5.30.14)
Let not your out-breath perish, nor let your in-breath be obstructed.
May Sūrya, as your sovereign lord, deliver you from death with his rays.
This tongue speaks within; it is bound, yet it stammers.
(5.30.16.c) Through you, I have cast out the wasting disease, the hundred swellings, and the fever.
(5.30.17’) This world is most dear to the gods and unconquered;
it is for this [world], O man, that you were destined for death when you were born here.
(5.30.17.e) And so we call upon you; do not die before old age.

‖17‖ (5.31.1’) The sorcery (*kṛtyā*) which they have placed for you in an unbaked vessel, that which they have placed in mixed grain, (5.31.1.c) and that which they have placed in raw meat—that I drive back again to them. ‖1‖

The sorcery (*kṛtyā*) which they have wrought for you in a cock or in a goat, or that which they have wrought for you in a woman wearing a head-ornament (*kurīrin*), that sorcery which they have wrought for you in a sheep— I take it back again.
The sorcery which they have wrought for you in a single-hoofed animal or in a many-toothed beast...
The spell which they have cast upon the donkey, that I take back again.
(3) The charm which they have placed upon the rootless *narācī* plant, or the spell which they have cast upon your field—that I take back again. (4)
The sorcery which the wicked have wrought for you at the *gārhapatya* fire, or even at the former fire,
and that sorcery which they have wrought within the hall— that I drive back against them again.
(5.31.5) The sorcery which they have wrought for you in the assembly hall, and that which they have wrought at the gambling place— (5.31.6)
The spell which they have cast upon the dice, that I take back again.
That which they have cast upon your army, that which they have cast upon the bow and weapons,
the spell which they have cast upon the drum— that I take back again.
That spell which they have placed for you in a well, or which they have buried in a cemetery;
that spell which they have prepared in your dwelling—that I bring back again.
That which they have made against you with human bones, and that which [they have cast] into the fire at the crossroads.
I drive back again that devourer of raw flesh, Mroka, who burns from within.
(9) We have seized her by the wrong path; we send her forth upon the right path.
The unwise man has seized her from the wise through his lack of understanding. (10)
He who attempted what he was unable to do, and broke his foot and toe— he has brought us good fortune, though he himself remains unfortunate among the fortunate.
May he be the performer of spells, the wielder of the *valaga* charm, the root-caster, and the one subject to curses.
(5.31.12.c) May Indra strike him down with a great weapon; may Agni pierce him with his missile!
(6.1.1’) Sing forth, O singer; sing mightily; bestow splendor!
(6.1.1.c) O Atharvan, praise the god Savitṛ!
Praise him who is within the ocean,
the Son of Truth, the youthful one whose speech is guileless and who is most gracious.
May that god Savitṛ indeed impel many immortal blessings for us.
(6.1.3.c) Both excellent hymns [serve] for a happy journey.
(6.2.1’) O officiating priests, press the Soma for Indra and run [to the sacrifice], (6.2.1.c) so that he may hear the singer’s word and my call. (1)
Into whom the drops enter like birds into a tree—into him with the soma-juice;
O Virapśin, strike down the malicious ones who possess demonic power!
Press out the Soma for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the drinker of Soma!
(6.2.3.c) May he, the youthful lord, the much-praised one, be victorious!
‖3‖ (6.3.1’) O Indra and Pūṣan, protect us; may Aditi and the Maruts protect us!
(6.3.1.c) May the Son of the Waters and the seven rivers protect us; may Viṣṇu and the Sky protect us! ‖1‖
May Heaven and Earth protect us for our aid; may the pressing-stone protect us, and may Soma protect us from distress.
May the goddess Sarasvatī, the fortunate one, protect us; may Agni protect us with his auspicious guardians.
(6.3.3) May the divine Aśvins, the lords of splendor, protect us; may Dawn and Night likewise grant us wide space.
(6.3.3.c) O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, Son of the Waters, increase our household for its complete well-being, even against all assaults.
(6.4.1’) May Tvaṣṭṛ, Parjanya, and Brahmaṇaspati [grant] my divine speech; may Aditi with her sons and brothers protect us now with invincible, rescuing power. (6.4.1.c) 1.
May Aṃśa, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Aditi, and the Maruts protect us.
May his hatred depart, driven away; may he keep the enemy at a distance.
O Aśvins, further our prayer; protect us, O wide-striding one, never failing us.
(6.4.3.c) O Father Heaven, ward off whatever misfortune there may be.
‖3‖ (6.5.1’) Lead him upward, O Agni, you who are invoked with ghee.
(6.5.1.c) Endow him with splendor and make him abundant in progeny. ‖1‖
O Indra, make him preeminent; let him be the master over his kinsmen.
Endow him with the increase of wealth; lead him to life and old age.
O Agni, cause him to prosper—he in whose house we prepare the oblation.

(6.5.3.c) May Soma speak in his favor, and may this Brahmaṇaspati as well. ||3|| (6.6.1’) O Brahmaṇaspati, whatever godless one plots against us, (6.6.1.c) subject him all to me, for the sacrificer who presses the soma. ||1||
O Soma, whoever, being ill-disposed, seeks to harm us who are well-disposed—strike him in the mouth with your thunderbolt; crushed, let him perish.
O Soma, whoever assails us, whether he be a kinsman or a stranger.
(6.6.3.c) Strike down his strength, as the great heaven does by means of its thunderbolt!
‖3‖ (6.7.1’) By that path on which Soma, Aditi, and Mitra go, O guileless ones— (6.7.1.c) come to us with that protection! ‖1‖

(6.7.3.c) Therefore, grant us protection!
‖3‖ (6.8.1’) As the climbing vine embraces the tree on every side, (6.8.1.c) so do you embrace me, that you may be my lover and that you may never depart from me! ‖1‖
(6.8.2’) Just as a bird, when swooping down, strikes its wings against the earth,
(6.8.2.c) so do I strike down your mind, so that you may be in love with me, so that you shall not go away from me. (6.8.3’) Just as these two, heaven and earth, the sun instantly traverses.
(6.8.3.c) Thus do I encompass your mind, so that you may be desirous of me, so that you may not turn away from me.
(6.9.1’) Long for my body, long for my feet; long for my eyes, long for my thighs.
(6.9.1.c) May the eyes and the hair of you who lust after me wither away through desire for me.
I make you cling to my arms, clinging to my heart,
so that you shall be in my will and follow my thought.
May those cows, whose navel is the place of union and whose heart is the charm of attraction— the mothers of clarified butter— bring her into harmony with me.
To the earth, to the sense of hearing, to the trees, to Agni the overlord—*svāhā*!
To the vital breath, to the intermediate space, to the birds, to Vāyu the overlord—*svāhā*!
To the sky, to the sense of sight, to the stars, to Sūrya the overlord—*svāhā*!
The *aśvattha* tree has mounted the *samī*; therein the rite for producing a male child was performed.
That indeed is the means of obtaining a son; that we bring now upon these women.
For the seed belongs to the man; it is poured forth into the woman.
(6.11.2.c) That indeed is the discovery of a son; Prajāpati proclaimed it.
(6.11.3’) Prajāpati, Anumati, and Sinīvālī have fashioned it.
Causing female offspring to go elsewhere, may they place a male here. (6.11.3.c) Causing female offspring to go elsewhere, may they place a male here.
Like the sun around the sky, I have come to the offspring of the serpents;
as the night [surrounds] the world, so do I ward off your poison from the *haṃsa*.
That which was known of old by the Brahmins, by the seers, and by the gods—[with that I ward off your poison].

Homage to the slayers of gods, homage to the slayers of kings;
and also to those who are the slayers of commoners—to you, O Death, let there be homage! Homage to your address from above, homage to your address from afar!

(6.13.3’) Homage to your sorcerers, homage to your remedies; homage to your roots,
The loosening of the bones, the loosening of the joints, the disease seated in the heart—
destroy all phlegm (*balāsa*) that resides in the limbs and in the joints. I drive out the phlegm from the one afflicted with phlegm, as I would [remove] a testicular swelling.
I cut his bond, his very root, like the urvārvā plant.
Fly away from here, O balāsa, like a swift, hornless young fawn! And so, like one whose year has passed, run away from here, you who do not slay heroes!
(6.15.1) You are the best of herbs; the trees are your attendants. May he who assails us be our attendant—[that is, may he be subdued]! (6.15.2) Whether kinsman or stranger, whoever assails us—
(6.15.2.c) May I become the highest among them, like the *talāśa* tree among trees.
(6.15.3’) Just as Soma is made the highest among herbs and the best of oblations,
(6.15.3.c) may I become the highest among them, like the *talāśa* tree among trees.
(6.16.1’) O fierce one, you are the devourer, the non-devourer, and the essence;
we devour the *karambha* offering for you.
(6.16.2’) Vihahla is the name of your father; Madāvatī is the name of your mother.
(6.16.2.c) You are indeed lost, you who have caused yourself to waste away.
(6.16.3’) O Tāvilikā, this Ailaba has caused us to waste away; Babhru and Babhrukarna, go away, O Āla! (6.16.3.c) Go forth, depart, O Āla! (3)
(6.16.4’) Alasālā and Lāsi are to the east, while Silāñjālā and Uttarā are to the north;
[and there is] Nīlāgalasāla.
(6.17.1’) Just as this great earth receives the embryo of all beings...
(6.17.1.c) Thus let your embryo be sustained for the sake of bringing forth after the birth.
(6.17.2’) Just as this great earth supports these trees,
(6.17.2.c) thus let your embryo be sustained for the sake of bringing forth after the birth.
(6.17.3) Just as this great earth supports the mountains and the hills,
so may your embryo be sustained for birth according to the impulse of Savitṛ.
(6.17.4) Just as this great earth supports the world established [therein].
(6.17.4.c) Thus let your embryo be firmly held for the sake of bringing forth the child.
(6.18.1’) The first onset of envy, and the subsequent one as well—
That fire in the heart, that burning grief, we extinguish for you.

As the earth is dead, more dead than the dead in mind; as the mind of one who has died is so, even so is the mind of the vigorous man dead. That which is settled in your heart, the mind that is prone to flight—
(6.18.3.c) Therefore, I release that envy from you, like steam from a leather bag.
(3) (6.19.1’) May the divine folk purify me; may the sages purify me with their wisdom.
(6.19.1.c) May all beings purify me; may Pavamāna purify me. (1)
May Pavamāna purify me for wisdom, for skill, and for life,
and also for safety.
O God Savitṛ, with both [means], by means of the filter and by means of the impulse, [purify me].
(6.19.3.c) Purify us so that we may see!
(6.20.1’) Like the flame of fire, it comes burning; like one intoxicated, it departs wailing.
(6.20.1.c) Let it seek someone other than us, some lawless one; let there be homage to Takman for its scorching destruction!
Homage to Rudra; homage be to Takman; homage to King Varuṇa, the radiant one.
Homage to Heaven; homage to Earth; homage to the plants.
O you who cause burning, you who turn all forms yellow—homage to you!
(6.20.3.c) To that ruddy, brown Takman who dwells in the forest, I pay homage.
(6.21.1’) Of these three earths, this ground is the highest;
from their very skins, I have gathered the remedy.
(6.21.2’) You are the best of medicines, the most excellent of plants;
(6.21.2.c) like Soma, like Bhaga in his journeys, like Varuṇa among the gods.
(6.21.3’) O wealthy ones, unassailable, desiring to win, may you win!
(6.21.3.c) And you are those that strengthen the hair, and indeed those that cause the hair to grow.
(6.22.1’) The tawny-winged birds, clothed in the waters, fly up to heaven along a black path.
They have returned from the seat of Cosmic Order; from there they have spread the earth with clarified butter.
Make the waters and the plants rich in milk and auspicious when you stir yourselves, O Maruts with golden plates upon your breasts.
Send forth nourishment and favor there where, O heroic Maruts, you pour out the honeyed mead.
O water-dwelling Maruts, send forth that rain which fills all the valleys.
(6.22.3.c) It moves like a gambler’s stake, like a maiden piercing the *tunnairu* cloth, like a wife for her husband.
(6.23.1’) Having flowed forth, those active ones have flowed day and night;
having flowed forth, I, whose resolve is excellent, invoke the divine waters.
May the waters, ready for the rite, release us from here for the sake of guidance;
may they immediately make the way clear for us to go.
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, let men perform their work.
May the waters and the plants be auspicious and gracious to us.
From the Himavat they flow down; their meeting place is in the Sindhu.
May the divine waters grant me that healing medicine which illuminates the heart.
Whatever pain has flashed in my eyes, and whatever [pain] is in my heels and forefeet—
may the waters, the best of physicians among healers, drive all that away.
O you who have the ocean as your consort, you whose king is the ocean, all you rivers that exist!
(6.24.3.c) Grant us the remedy for that; through it may we enjoy you.
(6.25.1’) The fifty-five [veins] that converge upon the neck—(6.25.1.c) let them all perish from here, like the curses of those who have been humiliated.
May those seventy-seven [veins] that converge upon the neck—
may they all perish from here like the spells of those who have been humiliated.
And those ninety-nine [veins] that converge upon the shoulders— may they [perish].

(6.25.3.c) May all those words of mine perish from here, like the insults of one who has been humiliated. (6.26.1’) O Evil One, release me; being self-controlled, have mercy on us! O Evil One, place me unswervingly in the world of the auspicious.
O Evil One, you who do not leave us—now we cast you out.
At the turning point of the paths, let another evil fall upon you.
Let the thousand-eyed immortal drive it away from us.

(6.26.3.c) May he whom we hate encounter [misfortune]; and him whom we hate, do thou indeed strike down. (6.27.1’) O gods, whatever the dove, sent as a messenger by Nirṛti, has come here seeking; for that let us offer praise and perform atonement. May the dove sent by Śiva be auspicious to us; O gods, may this bird be harmless to our home.
May Agni, the sage, accept our oblation; may the winged missile spare us.
(6.27.3) May the winged missile not harm us; it makes its nest in the place of fire.
(6.27.3.c) May he be auspicious to our cattle and to our men; may the gods not harm us here, O Dove!
(6.28.1’) With a verse, drive away the dove, casting it forth; rejoicing in the food, we lead the cow around.
(6.28.1.c) Enticing it away from evil places, let it leave its tracks and go forth toward strength, most skilled upon the path.
These men have served Agni; these men have led the cow around.
They have established their fame among the gods—who would dare to attack them?
He who first reached the downward slope, spying out the path for many—‖2‖

(6.28.3.c) To him who rules over these bipeds and quadrupeds—to that Yama, to Death, let there be homage! (6.29.1’) May the winged missile go down against those [enemies]; whatever the owl hoots, let that be in vain; or whatever footprint the dove makes in the fire. (6.29.1.c) Or whatever footprint the dove makes in the fire.

Those two messengers of Nirṛti who have come here to our house, whether uncommissioned or commissioned—let that place be devoid of both the dove and the owl. Let this [house] fly hither for freedom from enmity; let it settle here for the sake of heroic sons.
(6.29.3.c) Speak away; speak far away, following the distant direction.
(6.29.3.e) So that in the house of Yama they may behold you sapless, they may behold you as one who has become powerless.
(6.30.1’) The gods have plowed this barley, mixed with honey, upon the Sarasvatī, over the stone.
Indra, the lord of a hundred powers, was the master of the plough; the bounteous Maruts were the ploughmen.
That exhilaration of yours which is unshorn and dishevelled—by it you make the man one to be mocked.
From afar I shall cut down other forests than you; you, O *śamī* tree, sprout with a hundred branches.
O you with broad leaves, auspicious one, grown great by the rains, observer of the cosmic order! Like a mother to her sons, O Śamī tree, be gracious to my hair.
This spotted bull has come; he has settled before his mother.
And going forth to his father, he ascends to heaven.
||1|| He moves within the luminous realms; from his out-breathing and in-breathing, the Mighty One has manifested the sun. ||2||
He shines across thirty stations; the Bird has taken his stand.
Day by day, at the break of dawn, he pervades the days.
(6.32.1) Offer this into the midst of the forest-fire with clarified butter; it is the destroyer of sorcerers.
From afar, O Agni, burn against the *rakṣases*; do not let them scorch our houses.
(1) O *piśācas*, may Rudra shatter your necks; O *yātudhānas*, may he crush your ribs. (2) The plant of all-pervading power has brought you into the presence of Yama. (2)
O Mitra and Varuṇa, let there be safety for us here; with your flame, drive away the devourers who come from the front.
Let them find neither a knower nor a firm footing; striking one another down, let them go unto death.
He whose yoked [chariot] traverses this space, for whom men have generated the new light of heaven.
The lofty, delightful [glory] of Indra.
Unassailable, he is bold; daring and courageous is his might.
Just as in the past, his fame was unassailable, so too is Indra’s might.
May he grant us that wealth, vast and golden-hued;
Indra, the most powerful lord among men.
3 Direct your speech toward Agni, the bull of the peoples.
May he carry us across our enemies.
(1) Agni, who utterly consumes the Rākṣasas with his sharp flame— may he carry us across our enemies. (2)
He who shines forth from the furthest distance across the desert wastes—
may he carry us safely beyond our enemies. He who gazes upon all beings and beholds them together— may he carry us safely beyond our enemies.
May he carry us across our enemies.
(4) The bright Agni who was born on the far shore of this space—may he carry us across our enemies. (5)
May Vaiśvānara come to us for our protection from afar;
may Agni come to our well-spoken hymns.
May Vaiśvānara come to this sacrifice, united with us.
Agni [is the lord] among hymns and in times of distress.
Vaiśvānara has fashioned the laud and the hymn for the Aṅgirases;
may he bestow splendor and the light of heaven upon them.
We pray to Vaiśvānara, the observer of cosmic order (*ṛta*), the lord of the light of *ṛta*, the eternal heat.
He has fashioned all things; he, the controller, sends forth the seasons.
(6.36.2.c) Advancing the vigor of the sacrifice. 2 (6.36.3’) Agni, in the highest abodes, is the desire of all that has been and all that is to be;
(6.36.3.c) as the sole sovereign, he shines forth. 3
The thousand-eyed Oath has arrived, having yoked his chariot;
seeking out my curser, he comes like a wolf to the house of one who does not offer him.
O Oath, avoid us, burning us as fire burns a pool.
(6.37.2.c) Strike down here the one who curses us, as lightning strikes a tree from heaven!
(6.37.3’) Whoever shall curse us when we do not curse, or whoever shall curse us when we are cursing—him I cast back toward death, like a dog’s dreg of food thrown away.
(6.37.3.c) Him I hurl back toward death, like a dog’s dreg of food thrown away.
The splendor that is in the lion, the tiger, and the adder; that which is in fire, in the Brahmin, and in the sun;
the blessed goddess who gave birth to Indra—may she come to us, in harmony with our luster.
The splendor that is in the elephant, in the leopard, and in gold; that which is in the waters, in the cattle, and in men.
May that auspicious goddess who gave birth to Indra come to us, being in harmony with splendor.
In the chariot, in the axles, in the strength of the bull, in the wind, in Parjanya, and in the vigor of Varuṇa—
may that auspicious goddess who gave birth to Indra come to us, being in harmony with splendor.
(6.38.4’) When the drum resounds for the nobleman, in the prize-winning horse and in the wondrous power of man—

may that auspicious goddess who gave birth to Indra come to us, united with splendor. (6.39.1’) May glory increase through the oblation, impelled by Indra— a thousandfold strength, well-sustained, and produced by might.
(6.39.1.c) Increase me for the sake of preeminence, so that I may spread forth toward long-lasting vision, bearing the oblation.
(6.39.2’) With reverence, let us worship Indra, the glorious one, who is glorious with glories. May he grant us a kingdom impelled by Indra; in the bounty of you, the glorious one, may we abide.
Glorious was Indra, glorious was Agni, and glorious Soma was born;
glorious among all that exists, may I be the most glorious.
(6.39.3) May Heaven and Earth grant us fearlessness here; may Soma and Savitṛ grant us fearlessness. (6.40.1)
May the upper atmosphere grant us fearlessness, and may there be fearlessness for us through the oblation to the Seven Seers.
May Savitṛ bestow upon this village the four quarters, nourishment, prosperity, and well-being.
May Indra, free from enemies, grant us fearlessness; let the wrath of kings fall elsewhere.
Make us free from enemies from below, free from enemies from above;
O Indra, make us free from enemies from behind and place us free from enemies in front.
For mind, for consciousness, for intellect, for intention, and for thought—
To thought, to sacred learning, and to sight, let us offer worship with our oblation.
To the out-breath, the diffused breath, and the vital breath that bestows much nourishment—
to Sarasvatī of wide extent, let us offer worship with our oblation.
May the divine seers not abandon us—those who protect our bodies and those who are born from our own bodies. O immortals, attend upon us mortals; grant us further life that we may live.
I loosen the wrath from your heart, as one unstrings the bowstring from a bow.
(6.42.1.c) So that, becoming of one mind, we may move together like two friends.
(6.42.2’) Like two friends, let us move together; I loosen your wrath.
(6.42.2.c) We cast down upon a stone your heavy wrath.
I trample upon your wrath with my heel and my forefoot,
so that you shall not speak according to your own will, but shall follow my mind. This *darbha* grass is a dispeller of anger, for both oneself and for another.
This [mantra] for the one who has become free from anger is called the "Pacifier of Wrath.
||1|| This Darbha grass, which has many roots and stands reaching down to the ocean, having risen up from the earth, is called the "Pacifier of Wrath. ||2||
We draw forth the arrow from your temples and we lead away the one from your mouth,
so that you shall not speak according to your own will, but shall follow my thought.
The sky has stood firm, the earth has stood firm, and this entire world has stood firm.
The trees have stood with their sleep upright; let this disease of yours remain [there].
(1) The hundred remedies that are yours, and the thousand gathered together—[this is] the most excellent medicine for discharges, the best, the destroyer of disease. (2)
(6.44.3’) You are the urine of Rudra, the navel of immortality.
(6.44.3.c) Or you are named Viṣāṇakā; you have arisen from the root of the Fathers, the destroyer of the Vātīkṛta disease. 3 Depart far away, O evil-minded one! Why do you utter ill-omened things?

I do not desire you with my thoughts; wander among the trees and the forests. My mind is set upon my home and my cattle. Whatever we have committed through lack of control, through harsh speech, or through slander—whether awake or sleeping—may Agni cast all those evil deeds and unpleasant things far away from us.
O Indra, O Brahmaṇaspati, whatever we do in vain, may the wise Aṅgiras protect us from that misfortune and from distress.
O Sleep, you are neither living nor dead; you are the immortal embryo of the gods.
Varuṇānī is your mother, Yama is your father; your name is Araṅaru. (1) We know your origin, O Sleep: you are the son of the divine sisters, the agent of Yama.
You are the Ender, you are Death. As such we know you, O Sleep; protect us from evil dreams. (2)
Just as they pay back a sixteenth part, an eighth part, or a debt,
even so do we transfer all evil dreams onto our enemy.
May Agni Vaiśvānara, the maker of all and the source of universal well-being, protect us at the morning libation.
May he, the Purifier, bestow wealth upon us; may we be long-lived, sharing in the sacrificial draught.
(1) May all the gods, the Maruts, and Indra not abandon us at this second libation. Long-lived and speaking what is pleasing to them, may we abide in the good favor of the gods. (2)
This is the third pressing of the sages, they who by means of the *ṛta* set the chalice in motion.
May those sons of Sudhanvan, having attained the heavenly light, lead us toward a well-performed sacrifice and toward greater prosperity.
You are the falcon; the *gāyatrī* is your meter. I take hold of you.
(6.48.1.c) May it carry me safely to the conclusion of this sacrifice; Svāhā!
(6.48.2’) You are Ṛbhu, whose metre is the Jagatī; I take hold of you.
(6.48.2.c) May it carry me safely to the conclusion of this sacrifice; Svāhā!
(6.48.3’) You are the bull, whose meter is the Triṣṭubh; I take hold of you.
(6.48.3.c) Carry me safely to the conclusion of this sacrifice, Svāhā!
‖3‖ (6.49.1’) No mortal has ever reached the cruel part of your body, O Agni.
The monkey devours his own sharp point, as a cow devours her afterbirth. Like a ram, you move both together and apart when the upper and lower stones chew in the northern trough.
Crushing head with head and jaw with jaw, he devours the stalks with his green jaws.
The fair-winged ones have raised their voice toward the sky; in the mountain cave, the dark, impetuous ones have danced.
As they descend upon the appointed place of the lower world, they, resting in the sun, have deposited abundant seed.
O Aśvins, slay the devouring, jointless mole; split its head and crush its ribs!
"O you who have not eaten the barley, close your mouths; then grant safety to the grain!
O *tarda*, *pataṅga*, *jabhya*, and *upakvasa*—like a Brahmin at a sacrifice where the oblation has not yet been concluded, eat these barley grains without doing harm, and depart!"
O Lord of the waters, O Lord of the slaughter, you with the parching jaws, listen to me!
Those forest-dwelling predators, and whoever else you are that are predators—all of them we crush to pieces.
Purified by Vāyu’s filter, Soma has flowed forth, moving backward as he hastens across.
The ally and friend of Indra.
May the Waters, our mothers, purify us; may they who flow with ghee cleanse us with ghee.
For these goddesses carry away every defilement; from them I emerge bright and purified.
Whatever offense against the divine folk, O Varuṇa, men commit here through thoughtlessness, if we have violated thy law, O God, do not harm us for that sin.
Sūrya rises up from the sky, utterly consuming the demons before him.

(6.52.1.c) Āditya, visible from all sides upon the mountains, is the slayer of the unseen. ||1|| (6.52.2’) The cows have settled in their stall; the wild beasts have entered their lairs; (6.52.2.c) the waves of the rivers have subsided, and the unseen [spirits] have been smeared away. ||2||
I have brought hither the life-giving, wise plant of Kaṇva, renowned and possessing all healing powers; by it, mayest thou destroy those unseen [diseases].
May both Heaven and Earth, the two wise ones, and the bright, great [Soma], fulfill this for me through the sacrificial gift.
May Soma and Agni perceive our self-power; may Vāyu, Savitṛ, and Bhaga protect us.
May breath return to us, may the self return to us; may sight return, and may the vital spirit return to us.
May Vaiśvānara, the undeceivable protector of our bodies, stand within us against all misfortunes.
We have united with splendor, with nourishment, with our bodies, and with a gracious mind.
May Tvaṣṭṛ grant us wide space here; may he mend whatever in our bodies is injured.
This is that superior bond; I adorn Indra for success.
Increase his dominion and great glory, as rain makes the grass grow.
O Agni and Soma, uphold dominion for him and wealth for him;
establish him in the preeminence of the kingdom as the superior ally.
Whether he be a kinsman or a stranger, whoever assails us—
subject all of them to my will for the sake of the sacrificer who presses the soma.
The many paths leading to the gods that traverse the space between heaven and earth—
Whichever of them carries [the burden] without failing, to him may all you gods entrust me here.
(1) May summer, winter, the cool season, spring, autumn, and the rains establish us in well-being. May you grant us a share in cattle and progeny; may we abide in your windless shelter. (2)
(6.55.3’) To the *idāvatsara*, to the *parivatsara*, and to the *saṃvatsara*, offer great homage!
(6.55.3.c) May we abide in the benevolent favor and the auspicious goodwill of those worthy of sacrifice.
3 (6.56.1’) O gods, let not the serpent slay us, along with our children and our men!
May that which is closed not open, and may that which is opened not close. Homage to the divine hosts!
Homage be to the Dark One, homage to the one with transverse stripes! Homage to the self-born tawny one; homage to the divine hosts!
I crush your tooth against tooth, and I crush your jaw against jaw; I join your tongue with your tongue, and your mouth with your mouth.
This indeed is the remedy, this is the remedy of Rudra.
With that [remedy] by which one drives away the arrow with its single point and hundred barbs—(1) Sprinkle us with the *jālāṣa*, sprinkle us up with the *jālāṣa*!
The *jālāṣa* is a potent medicine; through it, grant us mercy so that we may live. (2)
May there be well-being for us and joy for us; may nothing whatsoever cause us distress.
May our sin be forgiven; may everything be medicine for us—may all things be medicine for us.
May the bountiful Indra make me glorious; may both these, Heaven and Earth, make me glorious.
May the god Savitṛ make me glorious; may I be dear here to the giver of the sacrificial fee.
Just as Indra is glorious between heaven and earth, and just as the waters are glorious among the plants, even so may we be glorious among all the gods.
Glorious was Indra, glorious was Agni, and glorious Soma was born;
glorious among all that exists, may I be the most glorious.
O Arundhatī, you first [came] from the oxen, and you from the cows.
Grant protection to the barren cow, to the bird, and to the four-footed beast.
May the herb Arundhatī, together with the goddesses, grant protection;
may she make the pen full of milk, free from disease for the cattle and for men.
I invoke the all-formed, auspicious, life-giving goddess;
may she drive far away from our cattle the missile of Rudra.
This Aryaman approaches from the east, with his top-knot loosened.
(6.60.1.c) Desiring a husband for this maiden, and a wife for the one who has no wife;
(6.60.2.a) She has grown weary, O Aryaman, going to the assembly of others. (6.60.2.c) Surely, O Aryaman, other women now come to her assembly.
The Ordainer has supported the earth; the Ordainer [has supported] the sky and the sun.
May the Ordainer grant to this maiden a husband who is desirable.
May the waters flow sweet for me; for me the sun has brought forth light.
To me belong all the gods born of fervor; to me has the god Savitṛ granted wide space.
(1) I have separated the earth and the sky; I brought forth the seven seasons together.
I am the truth and the falsehood that I speak; I encompass the divine speech and the people. (2)
I generated the earth and the sky; I brought forth the seasons and the seven rivers.
I speak that which is truth and that which is untruth, I who have delighted in Agni and Soma as friends.
May Vaiśvānara purify us with his rays, and may the wind, swift with its breath, purify us through the mists of the atmosphere.
May Heaven and Earth, rich in milk, observers of cosmic order, and worthy of sacrifice, purify us with their milk.
Seize upon the Vaiśvānarī, the true speech, whose expectations are bodies with smooth backs.
Praising her at our shared feasts, may we become masters of riches.
(6.62.3) "Take hold of the Vaiśvānarī for the sake of splendor; becoming pure, bright, and purifying, rejoice here in the common feast with joy, so that we may long behold the rising sun.
(6.63.1) "The bond which the goddess Nirṛti fastened upon your necks, that which was impossible to unloose—"
I loosen that [bond] for you, for the sake of life, luster, and strength; being impelled, eat food that provides nourishment.
Homage be to you, O Nirṛti of piercing brilliance! Untie the iron bonds and fetters. Yama gives you back to me; homage be to that Yama, to Death.
Thou hast been bound here upon an iron pillar by the deaths that number a thousand;
do thou, in harmony with Yama and the Fathers, cause this man to ascend to the highest heaven.
O bull-like Agni, thou gatherest together all the treasures of the noble one.

(6.63.4.c) You are kindled at the place of the *iḍā*; as such, bring us wealth. (6.64.1’) Agree with one another; be united; let your minds be in harmony, just as the gods of old, being in accord, partook of their portion.
The counsel is common, the assembly is common, the vow is common, and their thought is shared.
With a common oblation I offer for you; enter into a common consciousness. Common be your intention, and common be your hearts.
(6.64.3.c) May your mind be one and the same, so that you may dwell together in prosperity. (6.65.1’) Let wrath recoil, let the two arms, yoked by thought, recoil;
O Parāśara, crush their forward-flying vigor and bring wealth to us.
The "Handless" [weapon] from those who are handless, that arrow which you gods hurl—
by means of this oblation, I cut off the arms of my enemies.
Indra first performed the "Handless" [rite] against the Asuras.

(6.65.3.c) May my beings be victorious through the steadfast Indra, the Medin. (6.66.1’) May the attacking enemy be rendered handless; may those who come against us with their armies for battle be struck down. O Indra, strike them with a great weapon; let their plunderer flee, pierced through. (6.66.1.c) May their plunderer flee, pierced through. (6.66.1.c) May their plunderer flee, pierced through. "O you who stretch [the bow], who draw it, and who run while shooting—may you be rendered handless, O enemies; Indra has struck you down today.
May the enemies be handless; we cause their limbs to wither away."
(6.66.3.c) Now let us divide their sacred knowledge into hundreds, O Indra!
(6.67.1’) Indra and Pūṣan have moved along the paths on every side;
let those armies of our enemies be confounded today, far away!
Foolish enemies, you move about like headless snakes;
may Indra slay each one of you individually, you who are deluded by fire.
Bind the bull’s hide upon them; strike terror into the deer.
(6.67.3.c) Let the enemy flee away; let the cow come hither.
(6.68.1’) Savitṛ has come here with the razor; O Vāyu, come with warm water!
Let the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus, being of one mind, moisten [the hair]; O wise ones, shave [the hair] for King Soma.
May Aditi shave the beard; may the waters moisten it with luster.
May Prajāpati provide healing for the sake of long life and sight. With that razor wherewith the wise Savitṛ shaved the beard of King Soma and Varuṇa—
By that [power], O Brahmins, weave this for him: may he be possessed of cattle, possessed of horses, and possessed of progeny.
Whatever glory is in the mountains, in the Aragarāṭas, in gold, and in cows;
whatever sweetness is in the flowing liquor and in the mead—that [glory and sweetness] be in me.
O Aśvins, lords of splendor, anoint me with the honey of the bee,
so that I may utter speech full of luster among the people.
In me be radiance, and glory, and whatever milk belongs to the sacrifice.
May Prajāpati make that firm within me, as one makes the sky firm in the heavens.
Just as meat, just as liquor, just as dice upon the gaming board,
just as a man’s mind is struck with passion for a woman— so [is this].

(6.70.1.e) Thus, O inviolable cow, let your mind be fixed upon the calf. (6.70.2’) As an elephant follows step by step the track of a female elephant, (6.70.2.c) as a man’s mind, longing for union, is fixed upon a woman, so let your mind be fixed [upon the calf].
(6.70.2.e) Thus, O inviolable one, let your mind be fixed upon the calf.
(6.70.3’) As the rim, as the felly, as the nave is fastened to the wheel;
(6.70.3.c) as a man’s mind, when he is full of desire, is fixed upon a woman.
(6.70.3.e) Thus, O inviolable one, let your mind be fixed upon the calf.
(6.71.1’) Whatever food I eat in many forms— gold, horses, cows, goats, and sheep— whatever I have accepted as a gift, may Agni, the Hotṛ-priest, make that a well-offered oblation.
Whatever has come to me as an offering, whether formally presented or not, given by my ancestors and approved by men—
from that which my mind leaps up with joy, may Agni, the Hotṛ-priest, make it a well-offered oblation.
Whatever food I eat, O gods, whether by falsehood, or when intending to give, or when not intending to give, or when I promise it— [may Agni purify that].
(6.71.3.c) By the greatness of the mighty Vaiśvānara, may my food be auspicious and sweet.
(6.72.1’) Just as the dark [serpent] spreads itself out according to its will, fashioning its forms through the magic power (*māyā*) of the Asura,
so may this hymn of yours, O Śepa, by its force, join limb with limb together.

Just as the tail of a horse has been made thick by the wind, so may your tail grow as large as the tail of a wild ass. As great as the tail of a wild ass, of an elephant, and of a donkey, so may your tail increase.
(6.72.3.c) As great as is the vigor of the horse, so let your thigh increase.
(6.73.1’) Let Varuṇa, Soma, Agni, and Bṛhaspati come hither; let him come hither with the Vasus.
O kinsmen, all of you of one mind, approach the glory of this fierce lord.
Whatever vigor is within your hearts, whatever intention has entered your minds—that I sew together with oblation and clarified butter. O kinsmen, may your delight be in me!
Stay right here; do not depart from us. May Pūṣan make the path ahead difficult for you.
May Vāstoṣpati call out to you; O kinsmen, may your delight be in me.
May your bodies be united, may your minds be united, and may your vows be united. May this Brahmaṇaspati, Bhaga, bring you all together.
This is the appeasement of your mind and the appeasement of your heart;
furthermore, with that which is weary from the sun’s heat, I appease you.
Just as the Ādityas were united with the Vasus and the Maruts, being fierce yet free from malice.
(6.74.3.c) Thus, O consumer of the three foods, being free from malice, make these people here of one mind.
(6.75.1’) Drive that rival away from his home who attacks us;
with the *nairbādhyam* oblation, Indra has cast him down.
May Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, drive him to the furthest distance, from which he shall not return again for eternal years.
Let him go beyond the three distances; let him pass beyond the five peoples.
Let him go beyond the three luminous realms, from which he shall not return again for eternal years, as long as the sun remains in the sky.
Those who sit around him and prepare him for sight—
(6.76.1.c) Kindled by its tongues, let Agni rise up from the heart.
(6.76.2’) O Agni Sāṃtapana, for the sake of long life, I take hold of your station—truly, he whose mouth beholds the smoke rising upward.
(6.76.2.c) Truly, he whose mouth beholds the smoke rising upward. 2.

He who knows the fuel-stick of this [sacrifice] when it has been prepared by a Kṣatriya does not set foot upon the precipice for death. Neither those who pursue him nor those who lie in wait strike him down; he does not fall into their midst.
The wise Kṣatriya who takes the name of Agni for the sake of long life.
The sky has stood firm, the earth has stood firm, this entire world has stood firm;
the mountains have stood firm in their place, and I have established the horses in their station.
He who is the upward breath, the ultimate resort; he who is the out-breath, the right path;
the turning toward and the turning back—he, the guardian, I invoke him.
O Jātavedas, turn [them] back; let there be a hundred turnings for you.
A thousand are your returns; with them, restore us again.
By this true oblation, let this man swell once more;
let him cause the wife whom they brought for him to flourish with vital sap.
May he increase with milk; may he increase with royal power.
With wealth of a thousandfold luster, may these two be undecaying.
Tvaṣṭṛ begot the wife; Tvaṣṭṛ [begot] you as her husband.
May Tvaṣṭṛ grant you both a thousand lifespans and long life. May this Lord of the Cloud, the Increaser, protect us and grant us peerless prosperity within our homes.
O Lord of the Cloud, do thou bestow strength upon our homes; let nourishment come, and let wealth come. O God, O Increaser, thou art the master of thousandfold prosperity.
Grant us of that; bestow that upon us; may we be devoted to you for that.
He flies through the intermediate space, beholding all beings—by that majesty of the divine dog, with that oblation may we worship you.
Those three Kālakāñjas who dwell in heaven like gods—to all of them I call for help, for this man’s safety and well-being.
Your birth is in the waters, your abode is in heaven; your greatness is within the ocean and upon the earth.
With that greatness of the divine Śuna, we shall worship you with this oblation.
You are the restrainer; you extend your hands and drive away the demons.
Grasping offspring and wealth, this *parihasta* has become [your] companion.
O bracelet, hold fast the womb for the placing of the embryo;
O boundary-stone, place the son within it, and do thou bring him hither at our coming.
That bracelet which Aditi wore, desiring a son—
Tvaṣṭṛ has bound him for her, so that she may give birth to a son from the people.
I call upon the name of the one who has come, of the one approaching;
I invoke Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, the son of Vasu, the lord of a hundred powers.
"By that path on which the Aśvins brought Sūryā Sāvitrī, by that same path Bhaga said to me: 'Bring Jayā hither.
"O Indra, that great golden goad of yours, which bestows wealth—"
By that [means], O Lord of Might (*śacīpate*), bestow upon me a wife who shall give birth to sons.
O scabs, fly away like a bird from its nest!
May the Sun provide a remedy; may the Moon drive you away.
One is brown, one is falcon-colored, one is black, and two are ruddy.
I have grasped the names of them all; you who do not kill heroes, depart!
Asūtikā Rāmāyaṇī, the Apacit shall fly away.
(6.83.3.c) Glau shall fly away from here; that Galunta shall perish.
(6.83.4’) Accept your own oblation, being pleased in spirit; Svāhā! With my mind I offer this which is here.
(6.84.1’) Into whose terrible mouth I offer this, for the sake of releasing these who are bound.
People regard you as "the Earth," but I know you thoroughly from every side as "Destruction" (Nirṛti). (1) Be full of oblations for the living beings; this is your portion which belongs among us.
Release these and those from sin! Svāhā! (2)
Thus, O Nirṛti, release us; you who are not stingy, untie these iron fetters and bonds. Yama gives you back to me again; let there be homage to that Yama, to Death.
I am bound here to an iron post, summoned by the deaths that number a thousand.
In harmony with Yama and the Fathers, cause this man to ascend to the highest heaven.
May this divine tree, the *varaṇa*, ward off [the disease];
may the gods drive away the consumption that has entered into him.
By the word of Indra, and by the word of Mitra and Varuṇa,
and by the word of all the gods, we ward off your *yakṣma* disease. Just as Vṛtra held back these waters flowing in every direction, so do we restrain your disease.
(6.85.3.c) Thus, with Agni Vaiśvānara, I ward off your consumption.
(6.86.1’) A bull of Indra, a bull of heaven, a bull of earth is this one;
(6.86.1.c) a bull of every living being—be thou the sole bull!
The ocean rules over the flowing rivers; Agni is the master of the earth.
The moon rules over the constellations; may you become the sole bull. You are the sovereign of the Asuras, the preeminent one among men.

(6.86.3.c) You are the half-share of the gods; become the sole bull. (6.87.1’) I have brought you hither; you have entered within. Stand firm, unshakable. Let all the people desire you; let not the kingdom fall away from you. (6.87.1.c) Let all the people desire you; let not the kingdom fall away from you. (1)
Be right here; do not waver, like a mountain immovable. Stand firm here like Indra, and uphold the kingdom here.
Indra has established this one as firm with a firm oblation.
May Soma speak in his favor, and may this Brahmaṇaspati as well.
Firm is the sky, firm is the earth, firm is this entire living world;
firm are these mountains, and firm is this king of the people.
Surely King Varuṇa, surely the god Bṛhaspati, and surely Indra and Agni shall maintain your kingdom steadfastly.
Steadfast and unshakable, crush the enemies; cast down those who act as foes beneath your feet.
(6.88.3.c) May all the quarters be of one mind and united; may the assembly be favorable for you here, O steadfast one.
3 (6.89.1’) This head which was given as a gift, together with the virility of Soma—by that which has been produced from it, we cause your heart to burn. 1
We scorch your heart; we scorch your mind. Like smoke following the wind, let your mind follow after me alone.
To me you [belong], O Mitra and Varuṇa; to me the goddess Sarasvatī.
(6.89.3.c) May both ends of the earth cast thee into my very midst.
(6.90.1’) O Rudra, that arrow which thou hast discharged at thy limbs and at thy heart—
this very one we now draw away from thee today, turning it in every direction.
(6.90.2) Those hundred vessels of yours that are distributed throughout your limbs—of all those of yours, we summon forth the poisons.
(6.90.3) Homage to you, O Rudra, as you cast [the arrow]; homage to you when it is aimed.
Homage to her as she is being released; homage to her as she has fallen!
With eight yokes and six yokes they have ploughed this barley.
With that, drive away the disease from your body to the west.
Downward blows the wind, downward burns the sun;
downward the cow yields her milk—downward let your ailment go.
(2) The waters indeed are healers; the waters drive away disease.
The waters are the healers of all; may they provide healing for you.
Become one with the speed of the wind, O steed, when you are yoked; go forth at Indra’s impulse, swift as thought.
May the Maruts, possessors of all wealth, harness you; may Tvaṣṭṛ place speed in your feet.

(6.92.2) O steed, that speed of yours which is placed in secret, whether it be in the hawk or in the wind as it moves about, or that which is encompassed—(6.92.2c) with that, O prize-winning steed, being powerful through your strength, victorious in the contest, win the race, you who are swift in the assembly.
(6.92.3) O prize-winning steed, may your body, leading your own body, run for our benefit; may it bring us prosperity and protection for you.
Unassailable, the great god, for the sake of support, may he measure out his own light like a luminary in the sky.
Yama, Death, Aghamāra, Nirṛtha, Babhru, Śarva the archer, Nīlaśikhaṇḍa—
the divine hosts who have risen with their army— may they spare our heroes.

With thought, with oblations, with fervor, and with clarified butter, I pay homage to Śarva, to the King Bhava, and to those worthy of worship; I offer this salutation to them. May they lead the poison of evil away from us.
O All-Gods and Maruts, possessors of all wealth, protect us from the poison of evil and from slaughter!

May we abide in the good graces of Agni and Soma, Varuṇa of purified strength, and of Vāta and Parjanya. We bend together your minds, together your vows, and together your intentions. Those of you who are of contrary purpose, those we cause to bend toward harmony.
I seize your minds with my mind; follow my thought with your thoughts. I place your hearts under my control; follow the path along which I go.
Woven into me are Heaven and Earth, and woven is the goddess Sarasvatī.
May Indra and Agni protect me; may Sarasvatī grant us success in this.
The aśvattha tree is the seat of the gods in the third heaven from here;
there the gods obtained kuṣṭha, the manifestation of immortality.
A golden ship with golden moorings moved through the sky;
there the gods obtained Kuṣṭha, the flower of immortality.
It is the embryo of the plants, and the embryo of the Himalayas.
The embryo of every living being—make this one free from disease for me.
(6.95.3.c) The many plants whose king is Soma, possessing a hundredfold insight, impelled by Bṛhaspati—may they release us from distress. (6.96.1)

May they release me from the curse of the oath, and also from that of Varuṇa; and from the fetters of Yama, and from every offense against the gods. Whatever we have committed with the eye, with the mind, or with speech, while awake or while sleeping—
(6.96.3.c) May Soma purify these things for us by his own power.
‖3‖ (6.97.1’) The sacrifice is victorious; Agni is victorious; Soma is victorious; Indra is victorious.
(6.97.1.c) So that I may overcome all hostile armies, thus let us worship with this oblation at the Agnihotra. ‖1‖
(6.97.2) May there be *svadhā* for you, O wise Mitra and Varuṇa! Make the lordly power here swell with progeny and sweetness.
Drive Nirṛti far away into the distance; release us from whatever sin has been committed!
(6.97.3) Rejoice in this fierce hero; O friends, rally together after Indra!
(6.97.3.c) The conqueror of villages, the winner of cattle, with the thunderbolt in his arm, victorious in battle, crushing [the foe] by his might.

(6.98.1’) Indra shall be victorious; he shall not be defeated. As supreme ruler among kings, may he rule. Worthy of praise, worthy of invocation, worthy of homage, and worthy of worship, may he be present here.
(6.98.2) O Indra, you are the sovereign king, seeking glory; you are the one who has become the overcomer of men. You rule over these divine clans; may your dominion be long-lived and undecaying.
2 (6.98.3) O Indra, you are the king from the eastern quarter; O slayer of Vṛtra, you are the destroyer of enemies from the northern quarter.
Wherever the rivers flow, that is yours as conquest; you, O Bull, go forth from the right, worthy of invocation.
I call upon you, O Indra, from afar, even before distress comes near. I invoke the fierce one, the perceiver, the one with many names, the sole-born.
Whatever murderous weapon today rises up, seeking to strike down the army—there we place the two arms of Indra all around us.
We place the two arms of Indra all around us; may the Protector protect us.
(6.99.3.c) O God Savitṛ, O King Soma, make me well-disposed for my well-being.
‖3‖ (6.100.1’) The gods have given; Sūrya has given; Heaven has given; Earth has given.
(6.100.1.c) The three Sarasvatīs, being of one mind, have given this poison-destroyer. ‖1‖
O Upajīkas, that water which you gods poured upon the desert, by that which was sent forth by the gods, do you now corrupt this poison.
You are the daughter of the Asuras; you are the sister of the gods.
(6.100.3.c) Born from heaven and earth, you have made the poison sapless.
(6.101.1’) Be virile; breathe forth; grow and expand!
(6.101.1.c) Let the penis grow according to its proper measure; with it, strike the woman.
With that by which they urge the plough and with which they drive the sick man,
with that, O Brahmaṇaspati, stretch his legs like a bow. I stretch your legs as one stretches the string upon the bow.

(6.101.3.c) Step forth like a rishi toward the red steed, never becoming weary! I weary your mind as a king’s horse tires its back;
like a blade of grass severed by a gust of wind, let your mind coil itself around me.
Of *añjana*, *madugha*, *kuṣṭha*, and *nalada*—
(6.102.3.c) From the hands of Bhaga, I draw forth the swift prize of the contest.
(6.103.1’) May Bṛhaspati make for you a bond; may Savitṛ make a bond. May Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, and the Aśvins make a bond.
I bind together the highest, I bind together the lowest, and likewise I bind together those in the middle.
Indra has bound them all around with a cord; you, O Agni, bind them together.
Those men who come to battle, making their banners visible in ranks—[bind them].
Indra has bound them with a cord; O Agni, bind them together.
With seizing and with binding, we bind the enemies. We have cut off their out-breaths, and their in-breaths, and their very lives.
I have performed this seizing, sharpened by the Lord of Penance. O Agni, bring here those who are our enemies in this place! May Indra and Agni, and King Soma, the allies, strike them down!
May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, make the seizure [of wealth] for us from our enemies.
Just as the mind flies swiftly away according to its intentions,
so do you, O cough, fly forth, following the swift course of the mind.
Just as a well-sharpened arrow flies swiftly away,
so do you, O cough, fly forth along the expanse of the earth.
Just as the rays of the sun fly swiftly away, so do you, O cough, fly forth.
(6.105.3.c) Thus, O cough, fly away along the flow of the ocean!
(6.106.1’) At your coming and at your departure, let flowering durvā grass grow;
let either a spring arise there, or a pool filled with lotuses.
This is the gathering place of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean;
our houses are in the middle of the lake—turn your face away from them!
O house, we envelop you with the caul of ice.
(6.106.3.c) For our cold lakes have become [cool]; may Agni provide the remedy.
(6.107.1’) O Viśvajit, entrust me to Trāyamāṇā!
O Trāyamāṇā, protect all our bipeds and whatever four-footed property we possess.
O Trāyamāṇa, deliver me over to Viśvajit.
O Viśvajit, protect all our bipeds and our quadrupeds that are our own.
O Viśvajit, deliver me over to Kalyāṇī.
(6.107.3.c) O auspicious one, protect all our bipeds and whatever quadrupeds belong to us.
(6.107.4’) O auspicious one, entrust us to Sarvavit; (6.107.4.c) may Sarvavit protect all our bipeds and whatever quadrupeds belong to us.
O Medhā, come to us first with cattle and horses;
you come with the rays of the sun; you are worthy of our sacrifice.
I [invoke] the first Medhā, possessed of sacred power (*brahman*), impelled by *brahman*, and praised by the seers.

(6.108.2.c) Drunk by those practicing sacred celibacy (*brahmacārin*), I invoke her for the protection of the gods. That wisdom which the seers, the makers of beings, know as wisdom— O Agni, by that wisdom make me wise today.
Wisdom in the evening, wisdom in the morning, wisdom throughout the midday.
(6.108.5.c) We cause wisdom to enter through the rays of the sun by means of our speech.

||5|| (6.109.1’) Pippalī is the medicine for what has been cast away and the medicine for what has been pierced through; (6.109.1.c) the gods prepared it so that this [woman] might have sufficient life. ||1||
The long-creeping *pippalī* plants spoke together from the time of their birth:
"The living man whom we shall reach shall not come to harm.
The Asuras dug you in; the gods sowed you up again.
(6.109.3.c) A remedy for one afflicted by wind, and a remedy for one who has been struck down.

(6.110.1’) For you are the ancient one, worthy of praise at the sacrifices; as the Hotṛ priest from of old, sit here as both ancient and new. (6.110.1.c) O Agni, nourish your own body and win for us prosperity through sacrifice.
Born under Jyeṣṭhaghnyā, from the loosening of Yama’s bond, protect him from the uprooting of his foundation.
May he lead him across all misfortunes for a long life of a hundred autumns.
On a tiger-like day was the hero born; being born under a lunar mansion, he is a true hero.

May Agni appease your mind if it has been provoked; being wise, I prepare a remedy so that you shall not be driven mad. One driven mad by the offense of the gods, or rendered insane by a *rakṣas*—[I heal you].
Knowing this, I prepare the remedy so that you shall not be driven mad.
May the Apsarases give you back, may Indra give you back, and may Bhaga give you back;
may all the gods give you back, so that you shall not be driven mad.
(6.112.1) Let him not slay the eldest of these; O Agni, protect him from being uprooted by the source.
Being wise, untie the snares of Grāhī; may all the gods acknowledge you. (6.112.2) You, O Agni, loosen the snares of these three, by which they were bound in groups of three.
Knowing the way, loosen the snares that bind them; release all—the father, the son, and the mother.

(2) The snares with which the outcaste is bound, pinned limb to limb and cast up—let them be loosened from you, for they are meant to be released; O Pūṣan, wipe away the misfortunes of the slayer of the embryo. (3)
The gods wiped away this sin upon Trita; Trita wiped it away among men.
Therefore, if the *grāhi* has seized you, may the gods destroy it for you with their sacred power (*brahman*).
O Evil One, enter the rays of light and the smoke, or go forth to the rising vapors or the mists.
Perish along with the foam of the rivers; O Pūṣan, wipe away the misfortunes of the one who has killed an embryo.

(2) The twelvefold [sin] deposited by Trita, wiped away from men as their offenses—should the *grāhi* (seizing spirit) have reached you from that, may the gods destroy it for you by means of the sacred word (*brahman*). (3)
O gods, whatever offense against the gods we have committed,
O Ādityas, release us from that by means of the eternal Law (*ṛta*).
O worshipful Ādityas, release us here by means of the eternal Law.
When we, seeking to perform the sacrifice, O you who carry the sacrifice, tried to assist, we were not able to succeed.
(2) O all you gods, though sacrificing with fatness and pouring clarified butter from the ladle, we, though desiring it and striving to assist, were not able to succeed. (3)
Whatever sins we have committed, whether knowing or unknowing—
O all you gods, acting in harmony, release us from that! Whether waking or sleeping, if I have committed any offense, [release me from it].
Therefore, let both what has been and what is to be release me from that, as [one is freed] from a wooden post.
Like one released from a wooden post, like one who has bathed after perspiring and is cleansed of dirt,
like clarified butter purified by a strainer— may all the gods purify me from mental sin.
Whatever the cultivators, ignorant of food, first buried while preparing the furrow—this I offer into King Vaivasvata; may our food thereafter be worthy of sacrifice and full of sweetness.
May Vaivasvata grant us our portion; may he unite our share of sweetness with honey.
Whatever sin has come upon us sent by our mother, or whatever wrong our father has committed and caused us grief;
(2) whether this sin against the mind has come from our mother, or from our father, or from our brother, or from our son—may the wrath of all those ancestors who accompany us be auspicious. (3)
Whatever I have borrowed and not yet repaid, by which I move as a tribute-bearer for Yama—O Agni, through this [act] I become free from that debt; you know how to loosen all the bonds.
Remaining right here, we give this back; being alive, we deliver it to those who are alive.
(6.117.2.c) Whatever grain I have eaten after borrowing it, O Agni, by this I become free from debt.
(6.117.3’) May we be free from debt in this world, free from debt in the next, and free from debt in the third world.
May we dwell free from debt upon all paths—those leading to the gods and those leading to the fathers.
Whatever sins we have committed with our two hands, seeking to win the gain of the dice—
O Ugrampaśyā and Ugrajit, may those two Apsarases today remit that debt to us like a loan. O Ugrampaśyā, you who sustain the kingdom, may they remit to us these sins resulting from the play of dice.

(6.118.2.c) As one seeking to discharge a debt, may the tight cord not extend toward us in the world of Yama. Whatever debt I incur by not gambling, or whatever I promise, O Agni,
without intending to pay— may Vaiśvānara, our supreme protector and best of priests, lead us up to the world of the righteous.
I declare before Vaiśvānara whether there is any debt or a pledge made among the gods.
He knows how to loosen all these snares; may we then be united with what is cooked.
May Vaiśvānara, the purifier, cleanse me when I run toward a compact or a hope, unknowingly and begging in my mind—whatever sin is there, I drive that away.
Whatever harm we have done to the mid-air, to the earth, or to the sky, or if we have injured our mother or our father—
may this Gārhapatya Agni lead us up from that [sin] to the world of the righteous.
May Bhūmi be our mother, Aditi our place of birth, and the mid-air our brother, protecting us from imprecation.
Heaven is our father; may it be auspicious to us from the paternal side. Having reached my kin, may I not fall away from that world.
Where those of kind hearts and good deeds rejoice, having cast off disease from their own bodies—there in heaven, with limbs uncrippled and undiminished, may we behold our parents and our children.
O Horn, untie the snares from us—those of Varuṇa which are highest or lowest.
Drive away from us the evil dream and misfortune; then may we go to the world of the righteous.
Whatever [sin] you are bound for in wood, and whatever in rope, whatever you are bound for in the earth, and whatever in speech.
Therefore, may this Gārhapatya fire lead us upward to the world of the righteous.
The two blessed stars named Vicṛtau have risen;
may they extend for us the gift of immortality. May the release of the bound one go forth.
Open wide the world; release the bonds, you who set the captive free.
Like an embryo released from the womb, dwell along all the paths.
O Viśvakarman, first-born of Cosmic Order (Ṛta), I, the wise one, bestow this portion upon you.
(6.122.1.c) May we, following the unbroken thread given by us, cross over beyond old age.

(6.122.2’) Some cross over along the stretched-out thread for whom ancestral wealth has been given according to the tradition; some, having no kin, give and bestow it, and if they train themselves to give, that indeed is heaven.
(6.122.2.c) 2. If they train themselves to give, that indeed is heaven.
Take hold together, strive together; those who have faith attain this world.
Whatever cooked food has been served for you in the fire, for its protection, O husband and wife, take refuge together.
I, of common origin, ascend with fervor after the great sacrifice as it proceeds, following it with my mind.
(6.122.4.c) Invoked, O Agni, may we rejoice in shared revelry beyond old age in the third firmament.

(6.122.5’) These pure, purified, and sacrifice-worthy women I set down separately in the hands of the Brahmins. With whatever desire I sprinkle you here, may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, grant that to me. (6.122.5.c) May he grant that to me.
O you who share this dwelling place, I entrust to you this treasure which Jātavedas shall bring hither.
May the sacrificer follow after it in well-being; recognize him in the highest heaven.
O gods who share this dwelling place, recognize him in the highest heaven; find him here in this world.
The sacrificer shall follow after; make manifest for him his well-being, his sacrifices, and his charitable works.
(2) O gods, you are our fathers; O fathers, you are our gods. Whatever I am, that indeed I am. (3)
I cook; I give.
I sacrifice; may what has been given not fail me.
O King, take your stand upon the firmament; may this [offering] likewise find its place there.
Know us as those who have performed meritorious works, O King; as such, O God, be well-disposed toward us.

From the great heaven, from the mid-air, a drop of water has fallen upon me with its essence—O Agni, may I be united with sensory power, with milk, with the Vedic meters, with sacrifices, and with the deeds of the righteous.
If a fruit fell from a tree, or if it fell from the atmosphere, that is indeed Vāyu himself.
Wherever it touched the body or the garment, may the waters drive away Destruction far away.
(2) This fragrant unguent is prosperity; this gold is splendor and indeed purity.
(6.124.3.c) All purifiers are spread out above us; may Destruction and Enmity not cross over us.
(6.125.1’) O Lord of the Forest, may you be firm-limbed, our friend, a furtherer, and a hero of great prowess.
(6.125.1.c) You are bound with cow-hides; be firm! May your rider win all that is to be won.
Its power was drawn forth from heaven and earth; its force was brought together from the lords of the forest.
Worship with an oblation the chariot that is the vigor of the waters, encompassed by cattle, the thunderbolt of Indra.
It is the vigor of Indra, the vanguard of the Maruts, the offspring of Mitra, and the navel of Varuṇa.
(6.125.3.c) O divine chariot, graciously accepting this our offering of oblations, receive these sacrificial gifts.

(6.126.1’) Resound through the earth and the sky; let the world scattered in many places take heed of you. O drum, in harmony with Indra and the gods, drive our enemies far, even to the furthest distance.
(6.126.2) Roar forth strength; bestow vigor upon us! Resounding, drive away misfortunes.
O drum, ward off calamity from here; you are the fist of Indra—be firm! (6.126.3) Conquer this [enemy];
let them be victorious in the terrifying battle! Let the bannered drum resound loudly.

(6.126.3.c) May our horse-winged heroes fly together; O Indra, may our chariot-warriors be victorious!
