May those two arms of yours, those two forearms, those two shoulders,
and that hump of yours, yield for the giver curd, milk, ghee, and likewise honey. May those necks of yours, those shoulder-blades, those ribs, and those vertebrae [yield the same].
(10.9.20.c) Let them milk curd for the giver— milk, ghee, and honey.
(10.9.21’) Those two thighs of yours, the two knees, those two hips, and that which is your buttock—
let them milk curd for the giver— milk, ghee, and honey.
May that which is your tail, those which are your hairs,
your udder, and your teats, yield for the giver curds, milk, clarified butter, and likewise honey.
May those which are your shanks, your hocks, your dewclaws, and your hooves [yield the same].
(10.9.23.c) Let them yield for the giver curd, milk, ghee, and honey. (10.9.24’) O inviolable cow, that skin of yours which is in the *śataudanā* sacrifice, and those hairs of yours—
(10.9.24.c) let them yield for the giver curd, milk, ghee, and honey.
(10.9.25) Let your two haunches be two sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) sprinkled with clarified butter;
making these your two wings, O Goddess, carry the cooker to heaven.
(10.9.26) Whatever grain, even a single kernel, is in the mortar, in the pestle, on the hide, or in the winnowing basket—
Or whatever the wind Mātariśvan, blowing as he purifies, has shaken loose—that may Agni, the Hotṛ, make into a well-offered oblation.
(26) I set down separately in the hands of the Brahmins the divine waters, honey-sweet and dripping with clarity.
With whatever desire I sprinkle you here, may all that be accomplished for me; may we be masters of riches. (27)
Homage to you as you are being born, and homage to you once born;
homage to your tail-hairs, your horns, and to your form, O inviolable cow.
He who would know the seven downward slopes, he who would know the seven distant regions.
(10.10.2.c) He who knows the head of the sacrifice should take possession of the barren cow.
(10.10.3’) I know the seven downward slopes; I know the seven distant regions.
(10.10.3.c) I know the head of the sacrifice, and I know Soma, the far-seeing, within this [cow].
By whom the sky was protected, by whom the earth, and by whom these waters were guarded—
her, the cow of a thousand streams, we address with a sacred prayer (*brahman*).
(10.10.5) A hundred bronze vessels, a hundred milkers, and a hundred guardians are upon her back.
(10.10.5.c) Those gods who breathe within her know the cow as one.
(10.10.6’) Having the sacrifice for her feet, milk for her eyes, the *svadhā* offering for her breath, and the great world for her body,
(10.10.6.c) the cow, the wife of Parjanya, approaches the gods with the sacred word (*brahman*).
Agni has entered into you; Soma has entered into you by your will. Parjanya is your udder, O blessed one; the lightnings are your teats by your will.
You milk the waters first, then the fertile fields, by your will.
(10.10.8.c) You milk the third realm for food, its milk being at your command.
8 (10.10.9.a) When you, O observer of the cosmic order (*ṛtavarī*), arrived while being invoked by the Ādityas, (10.10.9.c) Indra made you drink a thousand vessels of *soma* at his will. 9
(10.10.10’) Since the bull called out to you from afar as you followed Indra,
(10.10.10.c) therefore the enraged slayer of Vṛtra took your milk and curd into his power.
{33} (10.10.11’) Since the enraged lord of wealth took your milk into his power,
This is that which today the Nāka protects in three vessels.
(11) The divine cow brought that Soma in three vessels to where Atharvan, consecrated, sat upon the golden sacrificial grass. (12)
For she has come together with Soma, and indeed with everything that has feet;
the cow has entered the ocean along with the Gandharvas and the Kalis.
For she has come together with the wind, and indeed with all winged creatures.
The cow danced upon the ocean, bearing the *ṛc* verses and the *sāman* chants. (10.10.14.c) For she has come together with the sun, together with every faculty of sight;
the auspicious cow has looked across the ocean, bearing the radiant lights. (10.10.15)
When you stood there, O observer of cosmic order (*ṛtāvarī*), enveloped in gold— the horse, having become the ocean, leaped upon you according to your will.
Then the auspicious ones, the willing, the instructress, and likewise *svadhā*, came together.

(10.10.17.c) Where Atharvan, consecrated, sat upon the golden sacrificial grass; ||17|| (10.10.18’) The barren cow is the mother of the Rājanya; O Svadhā, the barren cow is yours. (10.10.18.c) From the barren cow the sacrificial implement was born; from that the mind was produced. ||18||
The drop rose upward from the summit of the Brahman;
from there you were born by will, and from there the Hotṛ was produced.
The Gāthās became your mouth, and strength and will came from the Uṣṇih verses.
From his belly was born the sacrifice; from his breasts, O Lord, your rays were born.
(20) Your movement was born from your two shoulders, and your power from your two thighs.
From your intestines sprang the waters, and from your belly the plants. (21)
When you entered the belly of Varuṇa and came under his control,
then the Brahman called out to you, for he indeed knew your way.
All those who were in the womb trembled at your birth from the waters.
(10.10.23.c) For they say that she brought forth her; she is designated as *Vaśā* by the sacred hymns (*brahman*), for she is indeed its kin.
(10.10.24’) He alone who is the sole ruler of her brings [all] together through battle.
Sacrifices became the powers (*taras*); the *Vaśā* became the eye of the powers. (10.10.24.c) 24.
The cow accepted the sacrifice; the cow sustained the sun.
Within the cow entered the rice-mess together with the sacred word (*brahman*).
They call the cow immortality; they worship the cow as death.
By her will all this came into being: the gods, humans, asuras, ancestors, and seers.
(10.10.26.c) Whoever knows thus should accept the cow of plenty (*vaśā*).
For in this way, the sacrifice yields everything for the giver, without failing. (10.10.27.c)
Three tongues of Varuṇa shine within his mouth;
of these, she who shines in the middle is the cow, difficult to receive as a gift.
The seed of the cow became fourfold.
(10.10.29.c) Water is one quarter, immortality is one quarter, sacrifice is one quarter, and cattle are one quarter.
29. (10.10.30’) The Cow is heaven, the Cow is earth, the Cow is Viṣṇu, and Prajāpati.
(10.10.30.c) The Sādhyas and the Vasus drank the milk of the Cow. 30.
Having drunk the milk of the barren cow, those who are the Sādhyas and the Vasus indeed wait upon her milk in the realm of the sun. Some milk her for Soma; others wait upon her for clarified butter.
(10.10.32.c) Those who gave a cow to one who knows thus have gone from heaven to the third heaven.
(10.10.33’) Having given a cow to the Brahmins, one attains all the worlds; for in her is established the cosmic order (*ṛta*), as well as sacred knowledge (*brahman*) and ascetic heat (*tapas*).
(10.10.33.c) For in her is established the cosmic order, as well as sacred knowledge and ascetic heat.
On the Cow the gods depend for life, and on the Cow do men as well;
by the Cow all this has come to be, as far as the sun shines upon it.
